questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to tell a good joke to a large audience
Why children laugh much more often than adults
Famous comedians and their most popular TV shows
How laughing affects the body, in good and bad ways
questions.why: Neil says they're talking about laughter and how it could kill you, and Tim argues it's good for you.

questions.q: Why is Tim laughing at the start of the show?
options: Neil told him a joke before the show
Something the producer said made him laugh
He was watching a funny video on his phone
He choked on his water and started coughing
questions.why: Tim says it was 'something our producer said before I came into the studio'.

questions.q: How does Tim react when Neil says laughing could kill you?
options: He agrees and immediately stops laughing
He thinks it's a great joke and laughs even more
He says everyone knows laughing is good for you
He asks Neil for scientific proof of the idea
questions.why: Tim says 'That's not funny! Laughing is good for you – everyone knows that!'

questions.q: According to Sophie Scott, why can laughter be dangerous?
options: It squeezes air out and doesn't let you breathe in
It makes your heart beat much too fast for too long
It raises your blood pressure to a dangerous level
It makes you forget to eat and drink properly
questions.why: She says laughter squeezes the muscles so air goes out, and 'it does not want to let you breathe in'.

questions.q: What benefits of laughing does Tim mention?
options: It helps you sleep and lose weight
It makes you more intelligent
It releases happy hormones and reduces pain
It makes your lungs stronger
questions.why: Tim says the body releases happy hormones and people feel less pain after a good laugh.

questions.q: What did the research on laughter and pain find?
options: Any kind of laugh reduces pain
Laughing makes pain worse
Only children feel less pain after laughing
Big laughs reduce pain, but small chuckles don't
questions.why: Tim says a small chuckle doesn't act as a painkiller, but laughing a lot does.

questions.q: Why does Tim want to pinch Neil after his big laugh?
options: To test if the laugh made him feel less pain
To stop him laughing so loudly in the studio
Because Neil annoyed him with his silly joke
To wake him up because he looks very tired
questions.why: Tim asks to pinch Neil 'and test whether you feel any pain' after his guffaw.

questions.q: What does Tim conclude at the end?
options: Laughing is too dangerous for adults
We all need to laugh more
Children should laugh less
Neil is right about laughter
questions.why: Tim says 'we all need to laugh more' and Neil shouldn't say laughing is dangerous.
